newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says unaware of inspections at Daiwa Sec.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says unaware of inspections at Daiwa Sec.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) is unaware of any inspections of Daiwa Securities Co Ltd, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday.
Asked about market rumours that Daiwa had been inspected by Japan's securities watchdog, Ogawa said: "I have no knowledge of it whatsoever."

He added that the ministry was in charge of inspecting the financial health of securities firms, while inspections concerning transactions were handled by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC).
He also said individual inspections were not a subject to be discussed.
Daiwa said on Thursday that a check was being conducted by the SESC but it was just a regular inspection.

Brokers in the Tokyo stock market said on Thursday that shares in Daiwa had slipped after vague market rumours that the SESC was investigating the company over possible links with a "sokaiya" racketeer.
The market has become particularly edgy over any brokerage links with sokaiya since the scandal at Nomura Securities Co Ltd over suspected irregular deals.

On Monday, two Nomura directors resigned after the brokerage firm said they made apparently illegal deals and funnelled funds to a corporate client that has been linked by Japanese media to a former sokaiya.

Major Japanese asset management firms, including Nomura's own unit Nomura Investment Management Co, and major Japanese trust banks have suspended business with Nomura since the brokerage disclosed the suspected illegal deals.
Many firms have said they will wait for the results of a probe by the SESC before resuming business with Nomura Securities.
